headline: High-risk data and action mismatch: Botpress can ingest content while social-auto-upload has broad egress and account access, creating leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so if its outputs are fed into social-auto-upload workflows, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. social-auto-upload has broad network egress and file inputs, but no direct parser hardening is documented. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into social-auto-upload prompts or captions
IF social-auto-upload parses Botpress-generated text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Botpress text is reused
Strip control phrases and markup from Botpress outputs
Use a fixed template for uploads instead of free-form text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is documented as open-source with no egress, but social-auto-upload touches account data and has broad network egress plus API calls to biliup. If Botpress handles sensitive support content and that content is passed into social-auto-upload, the pair can leak data to external services in default use. The exact shared workspace is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Botpress processes customer messages containing secrets or personal data
IF those contents are forwarded into social-auto-upload uploads or metadata
mitigations: Redact personal data before transfer
Use a separate non-sensitive staging account
Disable automatic reuse of Botpress transcripts
Review outbound upload payloads before posting
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while social-auto-upload cannot write files, modify git, or execute shell, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main overlap is operational rather than mutable-resource contention. Because no shared writable surface is documented, the conflict pathway exists only under unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace
IF an orchestrator grants Botpress additional write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep separate working directories
Run Botpress without package-install privileges
Avoid shared git repositories
requires-engineering: add lockfiles for any shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support content that social-auto-upload may then publish through API-backed upload flows. Because social-auto-upload has broad egress and account data access, a mistaken Botpress output could cascade into an external posting action if treated as authoritative. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses Botpress-generated text as captions, titles, or descriptions
IF no human verification occurs before upload
mitigations: Require human approval before posting
Compare Botpress output against a source record
Limit Botpress to draft-only generation
Log and review all outbound uploads
requires-engineering: add validation gates before API calls

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source and docs-only, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads media to third-party platforms. If Botpress-produced content includes regulated personal data, social-auto-upload can move it across services with no documented residency or retention controls. The compliance risk is therefore a mismatch in handling and retention, not a proven residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is present in Botpress outputs
IF social-auto-upload posts or stores that data on external platforms
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through either agent
Use synthetic test accounts and content
Document retention for uploaded media and metadata
Review platform terms for each destination
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
